in.other_title: Code validation: all protocols modestly beat a solo verifier; nip and mnip gain about 11%
in.rationale: Anil et al. call for scaling Prover-Verifier Games to more challenging problems. Hammond and Adam-Day report that every protocol they test modestly beats a verifier trained alone in final test accuracy, with nip and mnip gaining about 11% and mnip best on worst-case performance.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether the interaction protocols Hammond and Adam-Day test improve over a verifier trained in isolation, as bearing on Anil et al.'s call to scale Prover-Verifier Games to more challenging problems

open_obligations: Check that grade-school math is 'more challenging' in the sense Anil et al. mean, given it has known answers.
Note that Kirchner et al. use helpful and sneaky provers; check how they differ from the prover in Anil et al.'s game.
Check how far from equilibrium the trained players are, since the cited passages give no equilibrium result.
in.other_title: Prover-verifier game training mitigates loss of legibility in LLM math solutions
in.rationale: Anil et al. call for scaling PVGs to harder problems and studying behaviour at approximate equilibria. Kirchner et al. propose a training algorithm inspired by Anil et al.'s Prover-Verifier Game that trains small verifiers and helpful and sneaky provers on grade-school math, and report that helpful-prover accuracy and verifier robustness increase over training and that legibility training transfers to time-constrained humans; the passages do not show whether this training reaches or studies approximate equilibria.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether prover-verifier game training scales to more challenging problems, for LLMs on grade-school math

text: The authors call for scaling Prover-Verifier Games to more challenging problems, including ones with no known verification protocol, and state that since exact equilibria are hard to solve for, more work is needed to understand prover and verifier behaviour at approximate equilibria; they warn that deploying PVG-trained systems before an equilibrium is reached could lead to unexpected behaviour.
title: Open questions: scaling PVGs to harder problems and behaviour at approximate equilibria
